run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. This
started in the last few hours. Please investigate the root cause using the
app-259-prod-logs index.

report.summary: No telemetry for the cluster the question names, production-us-east-2, was found in this Run, so the us-east-2 checkout 500s cannot be attributed to a cause from this evidence. The only log index available, app-259-prod-logs, is the single index in the registered Elasticsearch target and holds 9 documents; all 9 documents inside the authorized window are tagged cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2, and the whole-window aggregation returned no other cluster value (sum_other_doc_count 0). The errors that index does contain belong to production-eu-west-2: checkout-service logged 500s at 04:42:42Z ("circuit-breaker open for payment-service") and 05:12:42Z ("payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway"), payment-service logged 504 upstream timeouts on provider path /v68/payments at 03:42:42Z and 04:57:42Z, and a 05:37:42Z checkout-service line reports circuit-breaker half-open with 92% success. Those are observations about a different cluster and are not evidence for, and must not be read as the root cause of, the production-us-east-2 incident. Kubernetes access in this Run reads only the production-eu-west-2 cluster (8 namespaces; 34 pods including otel-demo checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d), so us-east-2 pod state was not observable. Jaeger (traces_list_services) and Prometheus (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on repeated attempts, so trace and metric signals — including any cluster label that could have located us-east-2 data — were not available. No root cause is named.

claims.text: The registered Elasticsearch target exposes exactly one index, app-259-prod-logs, with health green, status open and docs.count 9 (store.size 9.6kb); its mapping defines cluster, region, service, level, status_code, message, correlation_id and the date field timestamp.

In the window 2026-11-20T05:42:52Z to 2026-11-21T05:42:52Z, app-259-prod-logs matched 9 documents in total (total.value 9, relation eq), and the whole-window terms aggregation returned only cluster=production-eu-west-2 (9 docs) and region=eu-west-2 (9 docs) with sum_other_doc_count 0 — no production-us-east-2 document appears in this index in the sampled window; services present were checkout-service (6) and payment-service (3); levels ERROR 6, WARN 2, INFO 1.

The 9 documents returned (source_start_at 2026-11-21T02:42:42Z, source_end_at 2026-11-21T05:37:42Z, each cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2) are: 02:42:42Z checkout-service WARN "Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1800ms (target 800ms)"; 03:42:42Z payment-service ERROR 504 "Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms" (chk-eu-1142); 03:42:42Z checkout-service ERROR 500 "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s" (chk-eu-1142); 04:42:42Z two checkout-service ERROR 500 lines "circuit-breaker open for payment-service" (chk-eu-1208, chk-eu-1209; one states failure rate 38% > 25% threshold); 04:57:42Z payment-service ERROR 504 same upstream timeout (chk-eu-1220); 05:12:42Z checkout-service ERROR 500 "payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway" (chk-eu-1252); 05:27:42Z payment-service WARN "Payment provider degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=842"; 05:37:42Z checkout-service INFO "Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s".

The Kubernetes access in this Run sees the production-eu-west-2 cluster: 8 namespaces (app-100a, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo) and 34 pods across 4 namespaces, including otel-demo pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and app-100a pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-rdwgb; no production-us-east-2 object is reachable here.

The log evidence that does exist does not place any failure in production-us-east-2: every one of the 9 documents carries cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2, so the checkout 500 / payment 504 pattern it describes applies to that other cluster and cannot be cited as the cause or as impact evidence for the production-us-east-2 incident.

Hypothesis (unverified for the asked cluster): the mechanism visible in production-eu-west-2 — a degraded or slow external payment provider (502 and 30s timeouts on /v68/payments) tripping checkout's circuit breaker (38% > 25% threshold) and surfacing 500s on POST /api/checkout — may be the same mechanism behind the production-us-east-2 500s, but no us-east-2 log, trace or metric sample was obtained, so this is a lead to test, not a finding.

Obtain telemetry scoped to production-us-east-2 before any root-cause call: query that cluster's checkout and payment logs plus its Prometheus error-rate and latency series (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"} by status_code, and the payment RPC client duration/count) and Jaeger traces, and confirm the cluster/region field on each result.

If us-east-2 shows the same payment-provider timeout/502 signature, inspect that cluster's checkout circuit-breaker thresholds and the payment provider's status for that region, and check whether a fault-injection or failover setting is enabled for the us-east-2 checkout or payment workload.

gaps: No evidence of any kind was found for the cluster the question names, production-us-east-2: the only index (app-259-prod-logs) contains 9 documents, all cluster=production-eu-west-2, region=eu-west-2, and no us-east-2 document was returned inside the authorized window.

Prometheus was unavailable this Run: get_all_labels, get_metric_names (traces_* selectors) and execute_prometheus_instant_query (count(up)) each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate, latency and cluster labels from metrics could not be checked — this is a source outage, not a zero reading or proof of health.
Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error or dependency evidence, and no parent-child call edges, were obtainable.
Kubernetes access is limited to the production-eu-west-2 cluster, so us-east-2 pod status, container restart reasons and application logs could not be read.

The fetch_pod_logs query on otel-demo pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (containers: checkout; previous instance read through 2026-11-21T04:07:21Z with 3074 lines, current through 2026-11-21T05:40:22Z with 374 lines) returned status no_data: the regex error|fail|timeout|circuit matched none of the 3448 lines read, so this pod's runtime error content in the window is unchecked, not proven absent.
Whether production-eu-west-2 and production-us-east-2 share a payment provider, and whether the eu-west-2 degradation overlaps the us-east-2 symptom onset, is unknown.

In the accessible production-eu-west-2 cluster, 7 events were recorded inside the window (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint, Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate — all namespace app-100a, spanning 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z to 05:42:42Z); they belong to a different cluster and were not investigated as the cause of the us-east-2 incident.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deployment or config change history could be correlated with either cluster's behaviour.
next_steps: Route this P1 to the telemetry for production-us-east-2 (logs, Prometheus, Jaeger) and re-run the investigation there, confirming each result's cluster/region field before attributing it.
Check production-us-east-2 checkout error rate and p95 latency for POST /api/checkout and for the payment dependency call (RPC client count/duration, provider HTTP status) over the incident window.
Verify whether the external payment provider used by us-east-2 reported a degradation in the last few hours, and whether checkout there opened its circuit breaker as seen in the eu-west-2 logs.
Restore or re-register the Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints, then check whether their series carry a cluster label that includes production-us-east-2 data.

view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
